generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

  • Data: a collection of facts, figures, numbers, observations, or measurements that can be recorded and used to study or understand something.
  • Primary Data: data collected first-hand by the researcher for the specific study at hand (e.g., your own surveys, experiments, or observations).
  • Secondary Data: data that has already been collected by someone else for a different purpose, which the researcher now re-uses (e.g., a census report, a textbook, a newspaper).

questiondescription.text:
Daniel Murunga

Sources of data: matching the terms Data, Primary Data and Secondary Data to their definitions.

Ben (STACK audit)

Students match three statistical terms to their correct definitions using dropdown menus. Each dropdown shows the correct definition plus three distractors sampled at random from a pool of five. Terms restricted to those taught in the lesson (Data, Primary Data, Secondary Data); each wrong answer gives a diagnostic hint.

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

falsefeedback.text: Not quite. Data is the most general term: the raw facts, figures, or observations you record — not a chart, a conclusion, or a calculation done with them.
Not quite. Primary data is first-hand: collected directly by the researcher for this specific study. If someone else gathered it earlier, it is not primary.
Not quite. Secondary data was collected by someone else, for a different purpose, and is being re-used. If you gathered it yourself, it would be primary.

qtest.description: All three parts correct: full marks on every PRT.
All three wrong (a distractor selected): fires each F branch.
